title: Flare a copper tube in a precision flaring tool, step by step as its maker says
instruction: A short 3/8 in soft copper tube stands in the 3/8 opening of a precision flare tool's closed flaring bar, its end a little above the bar's top. The tool rests on two blocks; its yoke rests near the bar's hinged end (where along the bar varies), and its clamp screw and feed screw are loose. Flare the tube's end the way the tool's maker says: set the tube's end even with the top of the bar, slide the yoke over the tube with its arrow on the 3/8 line, tighten the clamp screw, then turn the feed screw handle clockwise (seen from above) until the feed screw's red top, standing up through the handle's hub, stops going down (the cone's clutch has released), then at least two more full turns. Then turn the handle back until the cone's tip is at least 2 mm over the bar's top (2.25 turns back from full depth), and move both grippers away from the tool and the tube.
context: Plumbers (510,600 US workers, O*NET 47-2152) flare soft copper tube for flare fittings: the CDA Copper Tube Handbook names the water service's connections at the main and the meter, and fuel gas lines. A precision flare tool forms the 45 deg flare. The skill is setting up the tool to its tolerances before the one-way forming: tube end even with the bar's top, yoke centred on the tube, clamp tight, then turned until the clutch releases and on to iron the flare. RIDGID EC42865: "Place the tube end even with top of flaring bar." "Align the arrow on the yoke with the appropriate line on the flaring bar" "Securely tighten clamp screw" "Once the clutch releases, turn the handle at least two more full rotations to ensure a uniform, smooth flare surface." "Loosen the feed screw to retract the flare cone." CDA Copper Tube Handbook: "Position the yoke with the flaring cone over the tube end and clamp the yoke in place." "Turn the handle of the yoke clockwise"
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top; clockwise is seen from above. Loose: the tube (0.375 in OD, 0.03 in wall, 75 mm long, 0.014 kg) in the closed bar's 3/8 opening, its end 4 mm over the bar's top, gripped by the bar. Fixed: the flaring bar, 7.5 in long and 24 mm deep, split along y at x 0.24, its top 85 mm over the table on two blocks; openings 1/8, 3/16, 1/4, 5/16, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4 in, smallest at the hinge pin (y -0.0953), the 3/8 opening's centre at y -0.0068 with a white line beside each opening and a 1.2 mm 45 deg countersink at the 3/8 opening's top. The bar's front half is hinged at the pin on a light closing spring (60 N m/rad, its half-hole 0.1 mm into the tube's place at rest) that presses its half-hole on the tube. The yoke slides along the bar (at rest near the hinged end: its middle 8 mm behind the pin, then 0, 4 or 8 mm further along by seed); a red arrow on its front marks the cone's axis. On it: the feed screw's handle (two wings 100 mm tip to tip, top 165 mm over the table, turning freely about z; the feed screw's red top stands up through its hub) and the clamp screw (along x, its head 55 mm in front of the yoke, its tip 0.5 mm off the bar's front face; a 100 mm T-bar through the head, its -y end 80 deg up; right-hand, 1.5 mm per turn, tightened clockwise seen from in front; its tip a 80 N/mm spring past contact). The cone's tip starts 2, 5 or 8 mm over the bar's top by seed and goes down 2 mm per clockwise turn of the handle (the screw's top sinks with it); its clutch releases 2.5 mm under the bar's top (the flare formed), after which the handle turns and the cone stays. While the cone presses the tube's end before the flare is formed, it pushes a loose tube down with 15 N (the closed bar's spring alone does not hold that); once the clamp is 0.4 turn past contact the model stops pushing (in the real tool the clamp holds the tube). A flare is formed once, where the tube's end stands when the cone reaches full depth. Tool sizes not in the sources are estimates from RIDGID's product photo.
scoring: The flare is good when the cone's axis was within 1 mm of the tube's at first contact and the tube's end was within 0.5 mm of even with the bar's top when the flare was formed (RIDGID's standard flare; above or below changes its diameter), the clamp tight (below) when the cone first met the tube, and the cone not brought over the tube from the side (its tip already more than 0.5 mm under the end); otherwise it is scrap. Ironed: 2 or more clockwise turns of the handle after the clutch released, counted while the clamp is tight. Retracted: the cone's tip 2 mm or more over the bar's top. Clamped: the clamp screw turned 0.4 turn or more past its tip meeting the bar. Set: the tube upright (its axis within 5 deg of vertical) in the 3/8 opening, its axis within 1.5 mm of the opening's, its end within 0.5 mm of the bar's top; on the line: the yoke's arrow within 1 mm of the 3/8 opening's centre. Clear: both grippers' collision hulls 10 mm or more from the tube and from the yoke's head, the handle's swing and the T-bar's swing. Still: the tube under 5 mm/s and it and the handle under 0.05 rad/s. Success (1.0, held 1 s): good flare, ironed, retracted, clear, still. Partial credit at the last step, each needing the one before: retracted, not clear or not still 0.8; ironed, not retracted 0.6; a good flare ironed under 2 turns 0.5; set, on the line and clamped, no flare yet 0.25; else 0. Scored 0 from then on: a scrap flare, the tube 30 mm below the table top, or the forming model not running (an error, or not stepping with the run).
reset_notes: The tube in the closed bar's 3/8 opening, its end 4 mm proud; the yoke at the seed's place, the T-bar up, the cone set to the seed's start height. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate. The clamp holds the tube by our model, not by contact: 0.4 turn past contact, the model stops the cone's 15 N push on the tube (a loose tube is pushed down). PhysX cannot form copper: the cone does not collide; the handle's turns set its height and the model records the flare (not drawn). No torque on the handle or T-bar; the clamp tip is posed from the T-bar's turns. The real bar has no spring: here a light one holds the tube until clamped. No flare nut. Sizes scaled from a photo.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 115.7 s, step 2,314)
